content.thinking:
I'm planning to write the whole file carefully in one pass without testing it first. I'm designing a koala clinging to a eucalyptus branch mounted on a wooden stand base, thinking through realistic proportions and how the koala sits in the branch's fork.

I need to work out the pose so the koala faces forward correctly relative to the model's +Z facing convention, deciding whether it hugs a vertical trunk or sits seated on a horizontal branch gripping a second branch in front. I settle on a seated pose on a horizontal fork with a vertical trunk and stand base, with arms reaching forward to grip the branch.

Now I'm positioning the specific geometry: the floor disc, trunk, seat branch at y=0.5 for the koala's hips, and upper branch for the arms to grip, along with estimated hip and chest coordinates for the sitting posture.

Positioning the gripped branch to avoid clipping the koala body, I'll simplify to a horizontal bar held by two curved arm-like supports from the trunk, forming a frame-like structure around the koala.

Simplifying further to a seat bar at the back with side branches curving up to a front bar, plus a trunk rising behind with leaf sprays. Now I'm defining the skeleton: hip root, spine chain rising through chest and neck to a forward-aimed head joint, sizing the koala's head as fairly large and round.

Working out proportions: head center around 1.12-1.14m up, body top near 1.28m with ears, roughly matching a real sitting koala's scale given the seat height. I'm setting up the body as a loft along the spine chain, defining joint positions from hips through chest to head using smooth curve points, making sure the root joint duplicates its position correctly at the start of the chain.

Now I'm placing the pelvis as the root joint, then adding a three-span spine chain, followed by a head joint aimed slightly upward and forward, and figuring out how the local coordinate system (forward, up, left) works for orienting the head and jaw naturally.

To simplify positioning, I'll define model-space coordinates by hand relative to a head center point, using explicit bone assignments to avoid confusion with local space, and I'm starting to lay out a grey fur color ramp for the palette.

Bumping paint resolution to 2048 for crisper fur detail. I'm planning the body shading logic so the chest/front reads cream via normal and position checks while the rest stays grey, with dithered edges for a natural transition. Then sketching the parts list, starting with a lathed base/stand with a wood-painted plinth, possibly a second tier.

Everything static needs a joint parent -- I'll add a "stand" joint parented to pelvis so the base rides along naturally if the koala moves. For the plinth itself I'm going with a boxy pixel-art wood plank texture (tiled 16x16) rather than a smooth cylinder, stacking a slightly smaller top slab over a wider base block to get that chunky plinth look.

Now I'm planning the trunk geometry: a swept path with cell-shaded eucalyptus bark coloring (grey-cream peeling strips with olive/rust accents), tapering from radius 0.07 at the base to 0.04 near the top, positioned behind the koala. I'm adding a horizontal seat bar for the koala to perch on, plus a connecting rod linking the trunk to the bar so the koala isn't just floating in front of it.

Now I'm adjusting the hip and spine coordinates so the koala's pelvis sits naturally on the bar without clipping too far through it, nudging the hip height to 0.66 and reworking the spine loft stations with their widths and heights up through the shoulders.

For the width/depth convention, I'm confirming that loft width maps to x and height maps to z-depth along the sweep normal, giving the body a 0.34-wide by 0.28-deep torso. Then I'm sizing the head sphere, placing its center around (0,1.17,0.13) and scaling it wider and flatter to read as a stylized koala head.

Now I'm positioning the head joint and aim direction for the model's kinematic chain, then designing the ears as layered spheres — a grey outer disc, a cream inner fringe offset forward, and tiny white spike boxes for fuzzy edges, rotated outward to face slightly forward-sideways.

For the face, I'm planning a protruding black box nose with highlights on the muzzle, a light grey ellipsoid muzzle beneath it, and tiny pixel-textured eye planes placed symmetrically, calculating their surface position along the head ellipsoid using the sphere's radius equation.

Now I'm thinking decals might work better than flat planes for the eyes, placing them directly onto the head surface with an outward-facing direction, and considering similar decal treatment for any head markings. For the fur texture, I'm planning cheek tufts as small triangular pixel-art cards scattered around the head sides and ears using a surface scatter function, though I still need to figure out how to tint or color these tuft textures appropriately.

Then I'm scattering cheek ruff cards filtered to the head's side-facing normals, using white tufts with a back/down lean, and planning a similar but larger scatter of grey body fuzz tufts with cream accents on the chest, applied over the body sweep surface. For the mouth, I'm adding a small dark decal under the nose on a separate lower jaw sphere part, scaled and positioned to join the head locally.

Now I'm defining the jaw joint parented to the head, separating the skull/muzzle/nose as upper parts, and shaping the lower jaw as a small cream sphere with a thin dark box decal for the mouth line. Then I'm setting up the shoulders near the upper spine and placing the hands gripping the front bar, building the forelimb using a limb function that bends the elbow outward and downward.

Checking the arm's reach: the distance from shoulder to hand is about 0.376, within the limb's total length of 0.44, so the elbow will bend naturally. I'm chaining the arm joints (shoulder, elbow, wrist) parented to the third spine joint, sweeping fur-covered radius along the limb, and preparing to add koala-style hands with opposed digit groups gripping the bar.

For the hands, I'm planning five digits per hand (likely two opposable thumbs plus three fingers), each as a short two-joint chain fanned out and curved to wrap over the branch, keeping the joint budget well within the 160 limit.

4 points with 3 spans works, so I'll go with 5 fingers per hand spread along the x-axis since the bar runs horizontally.

Working out the joint counts: 5 fingers times 3 joints times 2 hands gives 30, plus similar for feet gripping the bar. I want to simplify by trimming to 2 control points per segment where possible to stay under the budget.

Settling on three points per finger (base, over, tip) for a smooth Catmull curve, then attaching claws as small spikes anchored to the tip joint pointing outward.

The limb returns a 3-point array that works as a chain path, and I'm setting bend hints as a single direction applied to all inner joints, treating these as directions in model space.

I'm positioning the hand so the palm sits just behind the bar with fingers curling over the top front, checking the reach distance from shoulder to hand target comes out around 0.33 which seems reasonable, then working out the finger base and top joint coordinates.

Now I'm turning to the hind legs, placing hips and knees with legs spread forward, trying to figure out how the feet should grip the seat bar while the koala sits with legs dangling.

Still computing leg and foot geometry...

Still calculating toe curve geometry...

Now I'm checking the foot sole and ankle placement, then moving to the leg chain structure—hip, knee, ankle joints parented to the pelvis with appropriate thigh sweep radii.

Working out the hip-to-foot distance versus leg segment lengths, it's clear the knee bends sharply forward and upward into a squatting posture, which fits the pose I'm going for. Since this is a koala, I'll skip the tail entirely, maybe adding just a touch of fluff at the rump instead.

Now I'm designing the eucalyptus leaves as narrow blue-green pixel-art cards clustered around the trunk top and branch tips, each frame oriented outward with slight random variation to mimic natural pendulous growth, sizing them to match the long sickle-shaped leaf silhouette typical of eucalyptus.

I'll add small brownish-green gumnut spheres scattered along twigs, then build thin sweeping twigs from the trunk top with leaf clusters at their ends, including one on the front bar for the koala's food. For the bar structure itself, I'm placing the front crossbar along the x-axis and connecting it to the seat bar via side branches near the ends.

Still writing bar geometry...

I'm setting up the bark paint ramp with weathered browns and tans, adding rust and sage patches using noise for peeling texture and vertical grain streaks.

Now I'm building the wood plinth with pixelated plank textures, then defining the fur color ramp with noise-based variation and dithering, plus belly and chest shading for cream highlights on the body.

Limbs get grey fur with darker hands and feet painted separately. I need to keep flat color counts low since paints don't count against the palette limit, then snap colors to a consistent palette size before moving to eye decal textures.

Working out pixel art patterns for eyes and nose details, sized small and mapped onto the head geometry with a simple dark/light/highlight palette.

Now I'm positioning the muzzle and jaw spheres and boxes: muzzle centered around y=1.15 with a light grey gradient, nose placed just above it, and the lower jaw slightly below, leaving a gap between them to suggest where the mouth line should sit.

I'm adjusting proportions so the muzzle isn't too tall and the jaw doesn't overlap awkwardly, then slipping in a thin dark strip to represent the mouth gap between the two.

Now I'm working out the eye placement on the head sphere, calculating the surface position at the given x and y offsets so the eyes sit correctly on the curved face.

For details I'm planning a tiny eyebrow tuft, confirming the ear fringe is already handled via fur cards, and settling on fur paint colors—grey body with a lighter face, dark gray hands with cream claws as flat colors. I also note the head needs a bone joint assignment, then move on to setting up the base plinth with a tiled texture.

Now I'm designing the plinth as two stacked slabs with a trunk base ring, rigging a "stand" joint at the pelvis root, and making sure the trunk sweep is assigned to that bone before starting the trunk geometry with a catmull curve.

Still writing trunk sweep...

I should shorten the second branches to around ±0.5 so the overall width stays reasonable against the plinth, which I'll bump up to 1.1x0.7. I also need to add small leaf-covered twigs near the koala's reach and plan out a pixel leaf texture pattern for the foliage.

I'm defining a second leaf texture variant with slightly brighter colors, then working out how leaf clusters should be oriented on the branches—each leaf card hanging downward with a lean and bend to fake natural droop, generated via a helper that positions and orients clusters with some randomized spread.

For fur, I'm planning to use grayscale pixel-art tufts that get tinted by the part's color, alongside separately-colored gray and cream tuft textures to add ramp variation across the body, and sketching out the small pixel patterns for those tuft textures.

Still defining tuft placement and ear fringe cards...

Now I'm shaping the ears themselves as flattened discs with a darker outer layer and cream inner patch, positioning them symmetrically near the top sides of the head using the head's center and radius as reference, accepting some embedding into the head surface since exact placement isn't critical. Next I'm moving on to scattering fur tufts across the forehead and top of the head.

I'm giving claws a flat cream color, skipping detailed pad geometry for hands/feet, then working out the body skin loft so it follows the pelvis-spine bone chain, making sure the path handles overlapping joint positions at the start correctly even if the pelvis itself ends up without its own mesh span.

For fur paint, I'm shading the chest area with a cream tone blended using noise, letting the belly region naturally hide under the leg geometry, and applying a dark flat color for the hands and feet while skipping palm pad details for simplicity.

Now I'm setting up the joint hierarchy, assigning "spine" roles to the pelvis and spine chain, placing the head joint off the third spine segment with a "head" role, and adding a jaw joint as its child. I'm also inserting a neck joint between the spine and head to keep the rig anatomically reasonable, and considering ear joints parented to the head, though I'll likely skip detailed roles for those and treat them as simple bone attachments.

Setting up imports and module structure...

Defining more color ramps...

Still writing bark paint logic...

I'm defining color constants for rust and sage tones, plus hand, claw, and nose colors, then starting the koala builder setup with a 2048 paint size before moving into joint hierarchy construction.

Building the spine joint...

Now for the arms, I'm looping over both sides to compute shoulder and hand positions and generate a limb using bend parameters for a natural elbow curve.

Then I'm creating the arm chain with named joints parented to the spine, sweeping a tapered radius profile along it for the limb shape, and adding a palm sphere at the hand position to form the hand.

Now I'm working out finger placement around the hand, defining small jointed finger chains parented to the wrist with thin tapered sweeps and rounded caps, plus a small claw spike at each fingertip.

Then I'm moving to the legs, setting hip and foot positions for each side and building a thigh-knee-ankle limb chain parented to the pelvis, with the sweep radius tapering from a thicker hip to a narrower ankle.

Still writing foot and toe geometry...

Front bar spans the width with branching sweeps going up toward the sides, plus a rod connecting trunk to seat with flat caps and knots, and a diagonal brace for support. Now I'm starting the leaf cluster generation function...

Writing leaf placement logic...

I'll skip extra leaf clusters near the mouth and hands to keep it simple, and instead define branch curves for the right and left limbs with tapering radius, plus small twig rods sprouting from points along them. Then I'll scatter tiny gumnut spheres at various twig positions for detail.

For the trunk, I'm adding peeling bark strips as flat pale-colored decal cards scattered across the trunk surface with some lean angle, followed by small mossy tufts at the base of the plinth.

I'm also adding leaf litter boxes and a small brass nameplate with a pixel leaf motif on the plinth's front face, using a gold-and-dark border texture.

Writing wood tile code...

I need to remember to import the bayer dithering function, add nail dots at the tile corners, and figure out how to pass color for decal textures like the eyes.

Now I'm positioning the eye decal on the head part with direction and size, then considering whether to add brow or cheek shading decals -- probably skip those for simplicity.

For the nose I'm using a small textured box geometry positioned on the head, then sizing the head sphere's segment count.

For the muzzle, I'm using a cell-shaded paint function with a grey ramp palette to add lighting variation, then setting up the face scale and cheek tuft cards before working out how scatter placement count applies across the body sweep.

I'm filtering scatter hits by surface normal and position to split cream versus grey tufts, setting flow direction, then adding smaller tuft batches for the arms (14 grey) and thighs (12) while skipping tail and shoulder details to keep things simple. Now I'm finalizing the frame types for the output.

For the ear fringe I'm using a ring of points along the ear edge, letting it default to plain position/axis frames without a bone function, and defining the ear joints with parent, position, and aim targets pointing outward and up. I'm also settling on using plain number arrays for spine and other point lists since they satisfy the point input types directly.

Now I'm writing the jaw joint with its parent, position, and aim target, then checking limb return types and card/flow options before moving to naming conventions for toe and finger chains—using indexed unique names like `toe${S}${i}a` and `f${S}${i}a`—and setting sweep parameters like radius arrays and a reduced side count of 5 for the digit sweeps.
